elements.id-string-82: In this section, we recall several definitions and results on modulus sheaves.
elements.id-string-84: First we recall Suslin-Voevodsky's category of finite correspondences $\Cor_k$.
elements.id-string-85: It is an additive category having the same objects as $\Sm_k$, and its group of morphisms $\Cor_k(X,Y)$ is the group of algebraic cycles on $X\times Y$ whose components are finite pseudo-dominant over $X$.
elements.id-string-86: Fiber product over $k$ gives a symmetric monoidal structure on $\Cor_k$.
elements.id-string-87: For any morphism $f\colon X\to Y$ in $\Sm_k$, the graph of $f$ gives a morphism $f\colon X\to Y$ in $\Cor_k$.
elements.id-string-88: If $f$ is finite pseudo-dominant, then the transpose of the graph of $f$ gives a morphism ${}^tf\colon Y\to X$ in $\Cor_k$.
elements.id-string-89: We say that a presheaf $F\colon \Cor_k^\op\to \Ab$ is a \emph{Nisnevich sheaf} if for any $X\in \Sm_k$, the presheaf $F_X\colon U\mapsto F(U)$ on $X_\Nis$ is a Nisnevich sheaf.
